role.title: ICS Incident Responder
role.description: DRAFT. OT specialization of NICE work role PD-WRL-003 (Incident Response). Investigates and responds to cybersecurity incidents affecting industrial control systems, coordinating containment and recovery with operations, engineering and safety staff so that response does not cause unsafe conditions or unnecessary downtime.
role.overlaps_method: Computed: NICE roles sharing the most statements with this role, excluding the roles it extends.

citations.note: Parent NICE role; all its statements are inherited.

citations.locator: §3.3.8 Develop an Incident Response Capability (PDF p. 59)

open_questions: Should ICS forensics (controllers, field devices) be part of this role or only the separate ICS Forensic Analyst stub (PR-OT-014)?
Many responders are external (vendors, integrators, retained IR firms). Does the role need a service-provider variant?

statements.text: Skill in performing system recovery for control system environments

link.rationale: Inferred: System recovery for control system environments.

statements.text: Maintain backups of controller programs, configurations and firmware, verify their integrity, and test restoration

citations.note: Back up PLC logic and configuration; verify backups for reliability and integrity; test restoration. Firmware is a nice-plus addition.

statements.text: Coordinate incident response actions with operations, engineering and process safety staff before containment so that the response does not create unsafe conditions or unplanned stops

citations.note: Impacts of shutdowns or disconnects should be understood and communicated.

citations.locator: §3.3.9 Develop a Recovery and Restoration Capability (PDF p. 59)
citations.note: Prioritize human and environmental safety before restarting operations.

statements.text: Collect evidence from controllers, HMIs and engineering workstations (e.g., running programs, project files, device and application logs) without disrupting operations

citations.note: Analysis includes forensics and considering OT dependencies.

citations.locator: §3.3.8 Develop an Incident Response Capability (PDF p. 59)

statements.text: Restore controllers and OT systems from known-good backups and verify logic, setpoints and firmware before returning them to production

citations.locator: §3.3.9 Develop a Recovery and Restoration Capability (PDF p. 59)
citations.note: Restore to a pre-incident state; safety before restart.

statements.text: Knowledge of controller programs and engineering project files (e.g., IEC 61131-3 ladder diagram, structured text, function block diagram) as security-critical assets

citations.note: Treats PLC logic and configuration files as data to back up and protect.
Defines the controller programming languages; cited by part only.

statements.text: Knowledge of MITRE ATT&CK for ICS tactics and techniques

citations.locator: Appendix D.3.5 MITRE ATT&CK for ICS (PDF p. 218)

statements.text: Knowledge of OT containment options and their process consequences (e.g., isolating zones, disconnecting remote access, moving to manual operation, controlled shutdown)

citations.note: Mitigation may involve process shutdowns or communication disconnects that affect operations.

statements.text: Knowledge of OT incident coordination partners and reporting channels (e.g., equipment vendors, integrators, sector information sharing organizations, government agencies)

citations.note: Names OT technical support such as vendors and integrators among response contacts.

statements.text: Skill in reading controller logic (e.g., ladder diagram, structured text, function block diagram) to find security-relevant behavior such as hidden overrides or altered setpoints

citations.locator: Appendix C.3 Threat Events and Incidents (PDF p. 196)

statements.text: Skill in analyzing industrial protocol traffic to tell normal process communication from unauthorized commands

citations.note: A baseline of normal OT traffic helps separate attacks from transient conditions.

modules.objective: Identify unauthorized setpoint modifications in Structured Text.
Execute containment and recovery steps with process continuity and safety constraints.
Execute recovery steps and verify logic integrity after a controller reflash.
Identify MBAP header length anomalies in Modbus TCP traffic
Recognize a ENIP command and its direct physical consequence.
Analyze CIP service codes to detect unauthorized controller state manipulation.
Identify adversarial TTPs used for device fingerprinting via ENIP.
Analyze ladder logic to detect unauthorized changes.
Reconstruct an adversary timeline to identify unauthorized control nodes and tampered ENIP/CIP setpoints.
Identify adversarial TTPs for Profinet network discovery.
Detect unauthorized logic changes in Structured Text.
Identify the missing field in a truncated (Partial) MBAP header.
Reconstruct adversary timeline using historian and network layers.
Execute containment steps while maintaining process stability.
Communicate risk to leadership regarding network architecture.
Perform packet analysis to extract a setpoint modification.
Perform packet analysis to reconstruct a multi-state control change.
Interpret control logic and correlate behavior to a physical process.
Compare baseline vs modified logic state for hidden manipulation.
Identify a hidden logic override in a ladder logic comparison.
